messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1 - Cross-region routing anomaly detected: elevated 5xx across eu-west1->us-east1 fallthroughs starting now. Alerting on-call.
Alex: seeing a big spike in 502/503 from eu-west1 users to model endpoints. latency SLOs degraded ~4x.
Maria: graphs show request fanout to us-east1 increasing at 23:07 UTC. Heatmap attached (link). Could be a policy eval loop or stale pin propagation.
Alex: I can confirm route table churn around the same time, some routes briefly missing region pins.
Ryan (oncall): I'm on it — starting triage. First step: confirm whether DNS or our routing policy layer is misbehaving.
NetOps: our control-plane logs show repeated policy recalculations for geo-steering rules for eu-west1 at 23:06:58. Error: "policy-eval timeout" for several config shards.
Alex: running quick checks: `dig +short model-api.redwood.net @8.8.8.8` returns us-east1 IPs for eu-west users, TTL is 300.
Maria: also seeing KV cache evictions on routing service (OOM-ish) around 23:06. Could cause fallbacks to default region.
Ryan (oncall): mitigation plan proposal: 1) temporarily pin eu-west1 in the storefront route for affected customers; 2) restart routing-policy workers on eu-west1 shard (rolling); 3) lower DNS TTL to 60 if safe. Thoughts?
Alex: agree. Pin first to stop customer impact. I can submit a manual pin via admin UI targeted to eu-west1 for the affected model routes.
EMI (cust-succ): Customers reporting errors in EU — one on a paid Dedicated contract. Need a short external note asap.
Maria: pre-check: pin will take effect fast but we may need to flush edge caches. Also, if control-plane is unhappy, repeat churn could reintroduce misroutes after roll.
Ryan (oncall): Alex, go ahead with manual pin, annotate which routes, and add `rollback_after=30m` if we later revert. Maria, queue the restart for routing-policy workers in eu-west1, one at a time. NetOps, stand by to assist with any infra-side restarts.
Alex: doing manual pin now. Command shown in admin UI: `POST /admin/pin {"region":"eu-west1", "routes": ["/models/*"], "reason":"incident 2301234567 manual pin"}` -> response 202.
Alex: pinned. Admin UI shows pins active at 23:08:45.
Maria: starting rolling restart of routing-policy workers on eu-west1: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/routing-policy -n routing --selector=shard=eu-west1` (will do sequential pods).
NetOps: watching infra. No auto-scaling events, but one worker reported high GC cycles. Restarting should free memory.
Ryan (oncall): watching metrics — error rate for eu-west1-backed users dropping immediately. Nice. Latency trending back down.
incident-bot: Incident P1 created: ID INC-2301234567. Pager channel opened.
Alex: Flushing CDN/edge cache for pinned routes with `edgectl purge --path "/models/*" --region eu-west1` to reduce TTL surprises.
Maria: after first worker restart, policy recalculations returned to normal and no further timeouts.
EMI (cust-succ): logged initial customer impact to the ticket and notified the customer (they acknowledged). They requested ETA for full recovery.
Ryan (oncall): ETA: monitoring for 15 more minutes after rolling restarts and pin. If stable, we'll begin controlled rollback of manual pin and increase TTL back to 300.
Alex: capturing artifacts for postmortem: control-plane logs, routing-policy stack traces, kube events, and admin pin audit trail.
Maria: I see one suppressed exception in the policy evaluator related to config watcher retry backoff; looks like a bug where watcher retries build up under GC pressure.
NetOps: infra-level note: one eu-west1 host had very high memory usage due to a regression in telemetry agent; bumped to a new image which will roll out later. Might explain worker memory pressure.
Ryan (oncall): ok, status update for incident channel and ops: mitigation in place (manual pin + routing-policy restarts). Customer impact reduced to intermittent errors, majority flows normal. Proceeding to stabilize.
Alex: leaving a manual tag: `manual-mitigation: pinned-eu-west1; expires=23:38:45`
incident-bot: Reminder: oncall handoff scheduled in 4h.
Ryan (oncall): I'll do a handoff note once we declare stabilized. Maria/Alex — please keep logs in the incident folder.
Maria: agreed. I'll capture root-cause suspicion: memory pressure -> watcher retry storm -> policy eval timeouts -> fallback to default region. Will validate once full logs are in.
EMI (cust-succ): Customer asking if we will issue a status page postmortem. I'll coordinate language and send to Ryan for approval.
Ryan (oncall): Thanks. If we stay stable for 30m, I'll mark as mitigated and start post-incident steps. Handoff: next oncall is Zoe. @Zoe -- FYI you'll be on next rotation for this incident.
Alex: making a short runbook entry: `If policy-eval timeouts observed in eu-west1, pin region, restart routing-policy workers, check telemetry-agent for memory leak.`
Maria: saving heap dumps and GC traces for the workers that restarted.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2301234567 status -> MITIGATED (monitoring) at 23:10:28.
Ryan (oncall): marking mitigated. Leaving for Zoe: follow up on telemetry agent image rollout, validate watcher backoff fix, and coordinate postmortem writeup.
EMI (cust-succ): sent customer a brief update: we mitigated routing anomalies, working on root cause, will follow up with a postmortem. They said thanks.
Alex: closing the active pager thread but keeping artifacts.
Maria: adding labels: `region:eu-west1`, `cause:suspected-memory-pressure`, `mitigation:manual-pin,rolling-restart`.
Ryan (oncall): great work team. I'll start the post-incident checklist and ping SRE lead for RCA assignment.
